#4008. "Essentially Worthless" - Disgruntled Fans Are Review Bombing Pikmin 4 On Switch 2

Pikmin 4 - Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy is out now, bringing 4K visuals to the 2023 title along with the new Dandori Academy mode and some neat little extras like voice commands.

We awarded it a score of 7/10 in our review. It's still good – hell, the main Pikmin 4 campaign is possibly the best of the bunch – yet we can't deny our disappointment at the lack of mouse controls and 60fps performance.

But if you take a look on Metacritic, you'd think Nintendo just put out its worst game in years. Although the metascore is sitting at a commendable 83, the game's user score is much, much lower at 2.3. This essentially means its average is 'Generally Unfavourable'. Yeesh.

Most folks just seem disgruntled at the notion that Nintendo is charging for what they perceive to be a very minor upgrade over the original. It's true that a lot of games over the years have received free updates for newer hardware, but Nintendo has opted to charge £7.99 / $9.99 / €9.99.

"This switch 2 edition is essentially worthless. At worst it's a spit in the face of series fans. $20 AUD for a bunch of recycled content and 4k visuals. They couldn't even be bothered to implement 60fps even though the system could definitely handle it. Such a lazy update, and yet they have the gall to charge $20 AUD."

Meanwhile, another user provided a slightly more measured assessment, stating:

"The Dandori Academy has reused content, half of the maps so far are taken directly from the base game and the other half share the same exact layout. Plus the new card on the title screen looks like an ad, ruins the nice scenery, fortunately it can be hidden.

"The main game has also suffered, now somehow having longer loading times than it did on the original Switch. All other Switch 2 editions have made them shorter, so this is really weird. It's not a small difference either, some have literally doubled."

The comment about the load times is particularly interesting.

This has been highlighted elsewhere, with YouTuber 'Press A!' posting an analysis titled 'Pikmin 4's DLC is a disaster...' (flexing that signature YouTube nuance right there) in which he compares the load times of the Switch 2 Edition with the original. When exiting out of a cave, the original would take around 6 seconds or so to load the main environment, however the same moment took over 30 seconds in the Switch 2 version.

A few people have mentioned the load times being quite long, so we tested it out ourselves. While loading into a cave takes about 6 seconds, loading out took around 14-15 seconds. Not the 30+ that others are citing, then, but probably long enough to raise an eyebrow or two.

Pikmin 4's user score on Switch 2 is a startling contrast to that of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. Despite some concerns here and there regarding the game's overall difficulty and approachability compared to the original, Ocarina of Time commands the highest user score of all time at 9.6.

We'll be curious to see whether Nintendo takes any steps to improve the load times in Pikmin 4, but for what you actually get with the new content and visual enhancements on Switch 2, we'd say the upgrade price is probably appropriate. It'll tide us over until Pikmin 5, at least.

Review bombing as an act of protest is a valid act. As long as it stays within the boundaries of the piece of media that is being protested.

The consumer has a right to express when they feel like their trust was violated. If a collective giving a negative score on a product that they legitimately believe deserved better treatment is the only way to be heard, and any less extreme alternative would fall on deaf ears or cause the producer to learn the wrong lesson, it is the lesser evil to allowing a major corporate entity to have their actions go unchecked.

I can also think of much worse cases of review bombing. You want to know what actual irrationality looks like? I've seen cases of people review bombing entire franchises of media, not just the isolated bad eggs, because one entry was so overwhelmingly bad or had undesirable repercussions for the franchise. If that was what was happening here, I'd agree it was too far. But that is not the case.

I think there’s an interesting distinction being overlooked here: the difference between the intensity of someone’s disappointment and the actual quality of what they’re reviewing.

A 0/10 might accurately reflect how angry someone feels about Nintendo’s decisions, but does it accurately reflect the experience a prospective buyer can expect?

Reviews don’t just exist to communicate with devs and publishers. They also help other consumers make informed decisions. When we start using scores primarily as a form of protest, we’re compromising that purpose.

I understand wanting to send Nintendo a message. I’m just not convinced that making reviews less trustworthy is the best way to do it.

I agree that a lot of the Switch 2 upgrade-packs Nintendo are releasing should be free to current owners, and it would have bought Nintendo some necessary good-will from the fans.

But I also think this impotent display of fanboy-sulking is also pretty eyeroll-worthy.

I get that as consumers, we don't have a lot of great ways to make our dissent heard when a company does something bad; We can shout on forums/reddit, or we can "vote with our money" which is at best a silent demonstration prone to misinterpretation.

But review-bombing always struck me as the worst possible way to do it. Reviews are supposed to reflect a games quality to help other possible buyers, not be a metric to manipulate downwards in order to "punish" the developer. Kinda ironic that so many people who whine about metacritic-scores and reviewers "definitely being paid off or pushing an agenda" don't see the hypocrisy in what they're doing when they vote perfectly decent games down en masse.

I continue to share Logan Plant's (IGN) criticism of Nintendo's approach to the Switch 2 upgrades and the baffling inconsistency. The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom charged $10 for its enhanced version, but at least the improvements felt very substantial. On the other hand, Captain Toad: Treasure Tracker received a free update that added features such as 4K resolution, HDR support, 60 FPS performance, and a co-op mode.

That's why upgrades like this are frustrating. Nintendo is asking players to pay for enhanced versions, yet some of them still don't offer basic expectations like 60 FPS. Super Mario Party Jamboree is probably the most disappointing example. The asking price felt difficult to justify given what was actually included, and the fact that Nintendo couldn't even deliver a 4K presentation makes the value proposition look even weaker. For a paid upgrade, consumers should reasonably expect more meaningful technical improvements than what was offered here.

#4006. Xbox CEO Pens New Message, Urges Platform Not To Get 'Trapped' By Its Proud History

Yesterday, we talked about the Project Helix part of the Xbox 25th anniversary magazine that's been made available to read in full on the official Xbox Wire website, and there's plenty more interesting stuff where that came from!

For example, the magazine kicks off with a statement from Xbox CEO Asha Sharma, who discusses the past 25 years of the brand and where it's going in the future - similar to a statement she shared on social media recently.

This time though, she talks less about how games will be made, and more about the fact that she wants to take "creative risks" while also acknowledging that her team won't "get every decision right" along the way.

"There are plenty of milestones from the past 25 years, and you'll find many of them in these pages. But I don't think the story of Xbox is really a story about any given hardware, launch or number. It is a story about people. Players turned games into friendships, rivalries and family traditions. They played with roommates who became lifelong friends, with brothers and sisters who moved across the country, with parents who got older and kids who eventually picked up the controller themselves. Some of the people we played with 25 years ago are no longer here. Some are sitting next to us, now playing with a new generation."

"We should be proud of that history. But we shouldn't be trapped by it."

"Games are alive. The best ones find new players and new creators. They move between generations. They get changed, remade and occasionally broken apart and rebuilt into something nobody expected. Twenty-five years in, Xbox should have that same restlessness."

"We have been given the chance to care for some of the most loved games and characters in the world. Our job is to protect what makes them special without protecting them from change. To keep making new things. To take creative risks. To meet players wherever they choose to play. And to make sure someone discovering Xbox for the first time today can feel the same possibility that someone felt turning on that first console in 2001."

"We don't get every decision right. No company that is still making things does. But we can keep listening, learning and building. Twenty-five years ago, a relatively small group of people imagined that Microsoft could make a game console. It was an improbable idea. They made it real. I like that as our inheritance."

There's definitely some interesting stuff in here, including Sharma's insistence that Xbox shouldn't be "trapped" by its past, that her team should be willing to experiment and take risks in the future, and an admission that not every decision will work out for the best. That's pretty refreshing to hear, and it certainly reads well on paper at least.

Let's see what happens, eh? Xbox's 25th anniversary has been a weird year, full of ups and downs, but it seems like there's a cautious optimism circulating around the fanbase regarding things like console updates, exclusives and various other initiatives that have been introduced since the Xbox CEO took the helm at the start of the year.

These next 25 years are going to be fascinating to say the least!

#4004. All the hype has already made Crimson Desert one of the biggest launches on Steam this year

We're merely days away from the end of the first quarter of 2026, and Crimson Desert has come in clutch to join the list of big sellers.

Crimson Desert, the open-world action RPG off-shoot from Korean MMO Black Desert Online, has officially launched, nearly six years after it was initially revealed. The game has been building up a lot of momentum over the years, which recently coalesced to turn it into one of 2026’s most anticipated titles.

All of it has been leading up to this moment, and the game appears to have landed smoothly, though not without controversy, as has seemingly become part of its MO.

It has not been 24 hours since Crimson Desert launched on PC and consoles, and it’s already become a big hit. On Steam, one of two stores where the game can be purchased (the other being the Epic Games Store), the game shot to the top of the charts.

The action RPG continued to accumulate more and more players on Steam, peaking at a very respectable 239,045 concurrent players (via SteamDB). Though its success was very much expected, we perhaps didn’t predict its peak would be that high.

Indeed, Crimson Desert has been in Steam’s top 100 global sellers list for six weeks, jumping up six spots to become the number one seller this week just before it launched. As we get closer to the weekend, the numbers could climb even higher.

This peak concurrent puts Crimson Desert in the same league as several of the other major releases of the first quarter of 2026. The top spot continues to belong to Slay the Spire 2, which peaked at a staggering 574,638 concurrent players. It happened just days after the juggernaut Resident Evil Requiem achieved its own 344,214 peak concurrent, which was the year’s highest up until Slay the Spire 2’s release. All three are well ahead of Nioh 3’s 88,045 peak concurrent, and Marathon’s nearly identical peak of 88,337.

Crimson Desert has seen something of a mixed reception by critics. James gave it three stars in our review, saying it “lacks the connective sinew to be truly functional,” which is a common criticism shared by other outlets. Many also lamented the sheer number of systems fighting for player attention, its poorly explained mechanics, and counterintuitive controls.

On Steam, at least, players have similarly been divided, with the current Steam user rating sitting at Mixed, based on 8,728 reviews. Unsurprisingly, most of the negative reactions fall on the clunky controls and the game’s tendency to, as one Steam user put it, “so miserably tries to be everything at once, and fails to be anything at all.”

If you’re just getting started in Crimson Desert yourself, or plan to do so soon, we recommend reading these crucial tips to help orient yourself in the game’s vast world. You should also plan your initial skill unlocks by prioritising these skills to spend your Abyss Artifacts first.

#4003. Crimson Desert's first patch aims at fixing controls, but it mostly affects mouse and keyboard

The first post-launch patch for Crimson Desert is here, and the list of changes is promising, even if it doesn't go far enough to address some deeper issues.

Crimson Desert has been out for a few days now, and as positive as its been received by many players, the game suffers from several fundamental issues that anyone who’s played it has called out.

Perhaps the loudest one of those has been how the game controls, which is a problem that stems from the complexity of controls themselves, as well as the underlying animations behind many of the actions the player character performs.

In the first case, at least, something is being done.

Developer Pearl Abyss rolled out patch 1.00.03 for Crimson Desert on Monday. The patch is available now on Steam and PlayStation, with Xbox and the Epic Games Store following “at a later time.”

Today’s update follows a letter to players the developer issued on Saturday. The letter generally acknowledged player feedback, but specifically pointed to complaints about the game’s clunky controls as something of a focus for the team.

The action RPG has actually broken its launch peak concurrent player numbers over the weekend, though only by a few thousands more. Its Steam user review rating has also improved over the same period.

This latest update only includes an initial set of fixes, but Pearl Abyss vowed to keep working on addressing all other points of feedback. A highlight in 1.00.03 is the addition of a Storage at Howling Hill Camp, which can be used to store inventory items.

The most important changes, of course, affect how the game controls on keyboard and mouse. Pearl Abyss included several fixes and altered some of the default presets to make the experience less painful when playing the game with a keyboard and mouse.

There are sadly no changes to controllers, but it is something that the developer said we can expect to see in future patches. More improvements for keyboard and mouse setups are in the works, too.

Beyond the control changes, patch 1.00.03 also includes a set of gameplay tweaks, especially when it comes to enemy health and difficulty. It also makes fast travelling more convenient, and brings a few fixes to NPC dialogue. You can read the full change log on Steam.

If you’re deep in Crimson Desert already, we definitely recommend giving our guides a look. We recently added new pages to help you figure out where to socket your Abyss Gear, how to find Contribution Points - and where to spend them, as well as more generally helpful information like how to expand your inventory, and how to reveal the map.

#4002. Cleanser Man Is Mega Man: Dual Override’s Boss Design Contest Winner

Mega Man: Dual Override’s 2025 reveal brought back the classic boss design contest, asking fans to create and submit their own robot masters, with Capcom choosing one to include in the game. After thousands of submissions, we have our winner; meet Cleanser Man.

As his name suggests, Cleanser Man is a cleaning robot who attacks (and tidies) using a long, multi-cleaning hose arm. Capcom has provided the following character summary:

Cleanser Man is a cleaning robot with an obsession for pristine beauty. Fueled by an extremely sensitive dirt sensor, Cleaner Man’s ideal world is one without a speck of dust. However, his devotion to cleanliness has a cost. His aggressive scrubbing causes great damage to global landmarks and historic works of art. This fixation has caused the public to view him as more of a threat than a helping hand. Furious and feeling misunderstood, Cleanser Man seizes control of trash processing facility and uses it to pollute the environment with hopes of forcing the world to appreciate the importance of cleanliness.

Cleanser Man won out among the six finalists, a few of which were also cleaning-themed bosses. “In the end, we chose Cleanser Man because of the unique way the concept was brought together and the originality of the color design,” says game director Shinya Ikuta. “While staying true to and respecting the original submission, we adjusted certain details to better fit the world and style of the game.”  Unfortunately, Capcom has not revealed Cleanser Man's creator, but you can see the character in action in the reveal video below.

In addition to Cleanser Man, Mega Man: Dual Override's rogues' gallery includes the following revealed robot masters: Twinkle Girl, Jet Man, Tank Man, and Cook Man. The remaining three bosses have yet to be revealed.

Mega Man: Dual Override launches in 2027 for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, Switch 2, PlayStation 4, Xbox One, Switch, and PC.  To learn more about the game, read our extended preview here. You can also check out the game's recently revealed amiibo figures for the Switch versions.

#4001. Stalker 2’s first expansion officially revealed, and it's taking us to the power plant where it all began

Stalker 2’s first add-on isn’t far off, and it may just be the thing to bring you back to post-apocalyptic Chornobyl in 2026.

One of the biggest reveals out of today’s Xbox Partner Preview showcase has been the new Stalker 2 expansion. The developer did tease some sort of announcement ahead of the event, but I don’t think an expansion was on many of our bingo cards.

Cost of Hope is the big news; a new add-on that the developer has wisely decided to reveal fairly close to release. Or, at least, the planned release target.

First off, Cost of Hope is set for release this summer. It’ll arrive on all current platforms simultaneously, meaning PC, Xbox, and PlayStation. The expansion is described as “non-linear”, and it takes place in the heartlands, deeper into the Zone.

The story revolves around a conflict between Duty, and Freedom, two factions whose idea of the what the Zone is and their understanding of its possibilities differ widely. You’ll be playing as protagonist Skif once again, and the expansion’s events will run parallel to the main game.

GSC Game World says Cost of Hope will introduce two new regions, offering dozens of hours of gameplay. We’ll get to actually explore the Chornobyl Nuclear Power Plant as part of the expansion, alongside the Iron Forest.

Each of the two new regions will have its own hub area, NPCs, quests, activities and stories. Of course, it wouldn’t be a Stalker expansion without some new weapons, and Cost of Hope promises a few - some can even be seen in the trailer.

The developer also confirmed that there’s one other story DLC in the works. Together with Heart of Chornobyl, and Cost of Hope all three will form a trilogy of interconnected stories. More details on Cost of Hope - including a release date - will be revealed sometime in the summer.

#4000. "I Don't Feel This Is A Good Direction" - Chrono Trigger Composer Thinks It's Time To End Dragon Quest

"it’s no longer possible to create anything new"

Chrono Trigger composer Yasunori Mitsuda has posted a blog in which he states it might be time for the Dragon Quest series to end.

As covered by our pals over at Time Extension, Mitsuda-san believes that without Akira Toriyama – who sadly passed away in 2024 – the Dragon Quest franchise cannot continue imitating the iconic artist's signature style.

The catalyst for this comment was the release of a new mobile game titled Dragon Quest RPG: The Cursed Tree And the Chosen Isle, which features artwork strikingly similar to Toriyama-san's work.

“Dragon Quest RPG‘s Toriyama-san-styled illustration has become a hot topic, but for the illustrator, for Akira Toriyama fans, and for the now-deceased Akira Toriyama himself, I don’t feel this is a good direction for everyone involved. In my personal opinion, since it’s no longer possible to create anything new no matter how hard one tries, it might be time to end the Dragon Quest series, and for Yuji Horii to create a new RPG. (There are a lot of remakes out there, after all).”

Online speculation, highlighted by Power Up Gaming, also points at the potential involvement of generative AI to create the in-game characters. However, despite enthusiasm around the technology from creator Yuji Horii, there's doesn't seem to be any legitimate evidence that this is the case.

Regardless, Mitsuda-san does have a point. Dragon Quest is synonymous with Toriyama-san's art style, and it might be tricky to maintain this without the man himself at the helm. Indeed, reaction to Dragon Quest XII: Beyond Dreams hasn't exactly been universally positive, with some online users criticising the design of the main protagonist.

We think it's unlikely that Dragon Quest will end anytime soon, however. The series is still incredibly popular to this day, and continues to sell ludicrous numbers in Japan especially. Dragon Quest Monsters: The Withered World is scheduled to release on Switch 1 and 2 on 3rd December 2026.

News "It's Truly Astonishing" - Dragon Quest Creator Yuji Horii Made An AI-Generated Game In 30 Minutes

#3999. 'We've Heard You!' - Star Wars Galactic Racer Is Officially Adding Split-Screen Multiplayer

An incredible addition to an incredible game

Star Wars Galactic Racer is my favourite game of the year so far. It's an incredible racing title that even surpasses the original Star Wars Episode 1 Racer in my view, and I've had so much fun with the campaign and online multiplayer.

There's just one downside that everyone's been pointing out since it was revealed, and that's the absence of local split-screen multiplayer. With that in mind, the development team have found a way to implement it in a new update.

The update isn't available yet, but will be coming to the game in early 2027. Alongside it will be a new mode called Free Play, which is where you'll be able to freely choose your vehicle, character, planet and race track.

"We’ve heard you! Local split-screen multiplayer racing is coming in early 2027. A dedicated team at Fuse Games has been working hard to bring a brand new mode, Free Play, to STAR WARS: Galactic Racer. This new mode will allow you to choose your vehicle, character, planet, and race track to race alone or with up to 3 other players in local split-screen action."

It seems Free Play is the only place where you'll be able to access local split-screen multiplayer in Star Wars Galactic Racer, but that's no surprise considering how solo-focused the main campaign is. They'd literally have to rewrite massive portions of the campaign if they were going to implement split-screen into it.

Anyway, this is just an amazing bonus on top of an already amazing game, and I encourage you to check it out if you enjoy a title like Burnout 3: Takedown - it's fast-paced and frantic, has the same kind of takedown system that you'll remember from that game, and the roguelite campaign is really well designed (online is great fun as well).

If you've played it, let us know what you think of the game in the poll down below!

#3998. 2027 Video Game Grammy Nominations Include Avatar: Frontiers Of Pandora For The Third Time

Since 2023, the Recording Academy has included an official category for video game soundtracks, adding an air of legitimacy to a diverse musical medium we know and love. Today, we learned the list of nominees for the 2027 Grammy ceremony, and it's an interesting lineup. The nominations are as follows:

As is often the case, what stands out most about these nominees is how, generally speaking, they don't fully align with gaming culture's favorite soundtracks of the year, and instead often trend toward the most recognizable IP (often franchises with films) of the year. On that note, it's most surprising to see that Avatar: Frontiers of Pandora has been nominated for the third year in a row: once for the base game, once for the Secrets of the Spires DLC, and now for the From The Ashes DLC. None of these soundtracks are bad by any means, but their Grammy representation far outweighs their cultural footprint.

The standout here is Ghost of Yōtei, which is not an adaptation of the massive franchises the other games fall into. However, it's also a Sony-published game, which have a pretty good track record of getting nominations, potentially due to the company's massive presence in the music and film industries. Still, Ghost of Yōtei has a great, unique score that's deserving of its spot, and also one previously nominated for best music at the 2025 Game Awards. The Grammys accept any releases between October 1 of one year and September 30 of the following year, so Ghost of Yōtei barely made the cut for this window. The Game Awards nominees will be announced tomorrow – it will be interesting to see how much overlap there is between the categories.

This batch of Grammy noms also has fewer recurring nominees than past years. This is Gordy Haab's third nomination (he won in 2024 for Star Wars Jedi: Survivor) and John Paesano's second nomination (he was nominated in 2025 for Marvel's Spider-Man 2). It's also the first year since the awards' creation without Bear McCreary or Austin Wintory nominations.

Last year's nominations left a sour taste in the mouths of many, with several DLC nominees and a complete lack of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, the year's standout hit that many specifically praised for its music. This year certainly has snubs (Mewgenics, Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave, and Control Resonant all come to mind), but none as egregious as last year.

What do you think was the best video game score from the last year? Let us know in the comments!

#3997. Random: KFC Australia Staging Fake Funeral to Give GTA 6 Fans a 'Legit' Reason to Skip Work

GTA 6 mania has paved the way to some pretty wild headlines over the last couple of years, but now, as we approach the finish line, KFC might have provided the craziest yet.

In Australia, the fast food chain has announced it's holding a fake funeral in order to provide people with a plausible reason to take the day off work. Yes, really.

The company teased the event on social media platforms:

The funeral, for the dearly departed (and completely non-existent) Ann Alibi, will take place on 19th November, 11am AEST at the KFC in Robina, Queensland.

Attendees will be able to enjoy some free chicken at the wake.

Apparently, the service includes "a hearse, coffin, floral tributes, a book of condolences, an order of service and even a heartfelt eulogy delivered by a surprise guest."

If you can't attend in person, a livestream will be broadcast starting at 12pm AEST, and you can still claim that free food via delivery instead.

So, if you're an Aussie looking for an excuse to take 19th November off work, KFC's marketing stunt may be just the ticket.

This isn't the only business reacting to the imminent launch of GTA 6; some, such as Palworld dev Pocketpair, are simply giving employees the time off.

#3996. Never one to lag behind HSR and ZZZ, Genshin Impact will introduce its own new pink-haired animal-themed girl in Version Luna 6

Plus Mondstadt is expanding yet further north in Genshin Impact's Luna 6 update.

Today’s Genshin Impact Special Program has wrapped up, and it’s brought us some big news about the next major update. Luna 6 is the next phase in the action RPG’s story, titled Song of the Welkin Moon: Rondo - Augured Homecoming.

It’s set to arrive on April 8, bringing with it a tonne of new content, including a big expansion to the original region of Mondstadt.

As part of this new update, Mondstadt’s northern parts expand with new areas. The new Dornman Port is one thing, but the most exciting is the Temple of Space. This floating structure is home to Asmoday fragments, and is made up of different realms inspired by Liyue, Sumeru, and various other civilizations from around Teyvat. Launching with the update is a new mechanic that lets you manipulate the space to reveal hidden paths containing secrets.

If you take the time to explore, you’ll find a lot to there to learn about Asmoday, Ruler of Space. There’s a new boss to take on in the temple, too: Watcher: Fallen Vigil.

The only new character in Luna 6 is Linnea, who continues the current trend within HoYoverse games of focussing heavily on cute pink-haired animal-themed girls. Linnea is a 5-Star Geo Bow user who can really work with parties made up of Lunar-Crystallize characters, with her big gimmick being the ability to turn Hydro-Crystallize reactions into Lunar-Crystallize reactions.

Linnea has a companion, Lumi, who allows her to increase the Lunar-Crystallize damage she deals, while also lowering her enemies’ Geo resistance. Linnea can also deliver either off-field Geo damage or a Lunar-Crystallize reaction hit with her Elemental Skill.

Beyond that, she can heal the party using her Elemental Burst. If you take Linnea with you as you explore, she can help you discover rare animals, thanks to her innate naturalist abilities.

This update will also see Chasca get her first-ever rerun, and you’ll be able to roll for her in the first phase of Event Wishes. The second phase will feature no new characters and instead focus on Nefer and Lauma. There’s going to be another Chronicled Wish banner, this time specifically for Fontaine characters.

You can look forward to a few other new arrivals in Luna 6, including The Nod-Krai Trade Expo, some quality of life updates to Miliastra Wonderland to up the number of players in each lobby, not to mention various other UI changes.

#3995. Make Room For GTAVI By Deleting Your PS5 Trophy Clips

Hard drive space is a premium commodity, and its value has never been more apparent than in the approximately two and a half days leading up to the launch of Grand Theft Auto VI. The game is a whopping 209 GB, but thankfully you can purchase the game and preload it now – which you should do because who knows if the servers are going to be able to handle the strain of what is officially the most pre-ordered game ever on both PlayStation and Xbox platforms.

The easy (and likely necessary) answer is to delete the big games you aren't currently playing off your hard drive, but there is a cache of arguably unnecessary data on PlayStation 5 that might get you there before you have to make hard decisions.

You may have turned it off (Settings > Capture and Broadcasts > Captures > Trophies under the Auto-captures section > Save Trophy Videos under the Video Clips section > Change to None), which if that is the case, then I'm sorry. I can't help you. But the default setting which maybe you've never touched, is saving a lot of unnecessary video.

Every time you get a Trophy on PlayStation 5, it creates a short video clip that I bet you never have and never will watch. Here's how to delete all those videos fairly quickly to free up at least some space.

First up, go to the Media Gallery. The quickest way to do that is to press the screenshot button to the left of the touchpad, tap over to the most recent media capture on the left, press X, and then press the Go to Media Gallery button.

Next, go to the Trophies tab, go to the Sort and Filter option (the downward arrow with the three lines), and change Media Type to Video Clips.

After that, go back a few screens and go to the Select Multiple option (the overlapping squares with the check mark on it). Go ahead and press the Select All option, then press Delete, and then hold your breath and commit by pressing Delete again.

In taking screenshots to write this little article, I deleted 110 14-second clips. That's about 25 minutes of video footage, which ain't nothing. Maybe it will help you not delete that one game that you started three years ago that you are definitely going to get back to any day now.

#3994. Caleb's third Myth has finally arrived in Love and Deepspace, and it's good news for all the husbandbro fans out there

Love and Deepspace has kicked off a new event, squarely built around Caleb's new Memory Pair.

Love and Deepspace’s latest update is here, adding a new Memory Pair for Caleb. The event is dubbed Ghosts' Final March, and it’s available now as part of a new Limited Wish Pool, as it has always worked.

The new Memory Pair is a 5-Star Solar-Slot, which can be obtained through the aforementioned Wish Pool. Doing so will unlock the Netherlord Companion for Caleb, and there’s even more for you to explore in this one.

Alongside the big new Memory Pair, Ghosts' Final March also offers the opportunity to earn a new 4-Star Solar-Slot Memory Pair, alongside ten Deepspace Wishes, 500 Diamonds, and other freebies. The event ends on April 11, so you have some time to get in and play.

If you’re only interested in the 5-Star variants, you’ll be happy to know that Infold is sticking with 150 pulls as the absolute maximum to guarantee earning Netherlord. This will be automatically unlocked after you pull both Nether Yearning and Nether Parting through the Wish Pool.

Obtaining either of the two will give you access to all chapters for the new Myth that’s also available as part of this event: Yin Yang Sundering. You can read all the lore once either of the two Memories have been unlocked, and you won’t even need to upgrade either of them.

The Lost Souls event has also kicked off alongside the new update. You can take part to claim a 4-Star Solar Slor Memory Pair for Caleb: Duskshard Dreams and Duskshard Lotus. You can also earn the 3-Star Memory, Lotus Bond, alongside some other freebies like more Wishes, Diamonds, Photo Poses, and an event-exclusive title.

#3993. Poll: What Do You Think The Metacritic Score Will Be For GTA 6?

Considering we're just a few days away from the release of GTA 6 on November 19th, we're bound to start getting reviews at some point between now and launch, and it'll be fascinating to see what the critics think of it!

This is a series that has consistently dominated on Metacritic over the years - a website that takes loads of professional reviews and creates an average score based around them. Grand Theft Auto V has a 97 average rating on there, for example, while GTA 4 goes even higher with a 98 rating.

In fact, every mainline release since GTA 3 (not including stuff like Chinatown Wars and Liberty City Stories) has reached at least a 95 on the platform. To put that into context, the best-rated Xbox Series X game of the year on Metacritic right now is Hades 2, and that game has a 95 average rating.

Feature These Are Xbox's Best 25 Games From 2001-2026 According To Metacritic

If we're going off history alone, GTA 6 has every chance of becoming the highest-reviewed game of 2026 on Xbox and PS5. The question is whether it'll manage to hit those highs once again, or whether it'll struggle to meet the hype.

Let's not forget there's never been a wait like this for a GTA game before, and while absence definitely does make the heart grow fonder, it also creates a sense of expectation that's extremely difficult to live up to.

We'll have to wait and see what happens! You'll find a review roundup on Pure Xbox ASAP, and it seems the smart bet is at least a 95 rating on Metacritic, although that's much easier said than achieved.

#3992. Review: TANUKI: Pon's Summer (Switch 2) - Cosy Postie Delivers Sick BMX Tricks & Minigames

The gaming calendar is busier than it’s been in recent memory. We’re wedged between the Ocarina of Time remake and GTA 6, having only just recovered from the onslaught of games that launched in September. The prospect of picking up another right now might not be an inviting one, but if any game could do it, it’s Tanuki: Pon’s Summer.

This quiet, cosy, understated gem has really launched at the perfect time. Playing as the titular Tanuki, you’re tasked with getting a shrine ready for a big festival towards the end of the summer. You have to raise funds for repair work, and find folks in town who can actually carry it out. To do so, you pick up a delivery job, get to know all of your eccentric neighbours, and pull off some sick BMX tricks along the way.

That sounds simple, but this is just the ramp used to propel you into the ridiculous amount of tasks you can get up to in Tanuki: Pon’s Summer. While primarily all about riding a BMX and delivering parcels, you quickly realise that this is a simulation game with a vibrant, animated world that invites exploration.

A quirk of the delivery outfit you work for is that you don’t just deliver the mail. No, you are the backbone of society. The job isn’t over until the customer has a smile on their face. So, if your round takes you to a local fisherman, and he’s feeling down about how he isn’t getting enough business, it’s your job to cheer him up and try out some fishing yourself. If you’re dropping a parcel off at a bar, and the place is packed, you better get ready to pull pints. If a photographer is lacking inspiration, then you have to pick up a camera and help her find it.

You get the point; Tanuki: Pon’s Summer manages to pull off so many wildly different minigames with ease, and (mostly) without losing its identity. When you park up the BMX to play some baseball, it feels like you’re diving further into this gorgeous world, rather than stepping into a different game entirely.

It feels like the idea behind these minigames is that they’re not supposed to overstay their welcome, but I found myself sorely wishing I could return to a few of them. The golf minigame towards the end in particular is one of the best golf sims going. The same goes for bar work; trying to replicate the drinks being ordered was satisfying and moreish, but gone too soon and never playable again. If anything, developer Denkiworks misses a trick in not giving you some kind of game mode that lets you play through these on a loop - I would have happily dived back in for that.

This is not to say that every minigame is pulled off with ease. There are some that just don’t work, and were more of a frustrating slog than anything else. The good thing is that this is a cosy game with low stakes, so if you’re struggling with one of them, there’s almost always a way to make things more generous, or skip over it if you fail enough times. But at times, this can feel like a cop out; the few frustrating minigames could have been improved rather than skipped over.

Unfortunately, the worst game of the bunch doesn’t even let you skip it, at least in my playthrough. This involves you transporting boulders in a cave, rolling them through an obstacle course.

To understand the issue with this, you have to understand that Tanuki: Pon's Summer doesn’t do precise controls. The opening makes this clear when you’re taught how to use the BMX - everything is simplified, and you’re not expected to do anything too intricate. Pon moves around too sluggishly and ragdoll-y for that to work. And for the most part, the game is built around this.

The cave minigame forgets this entirely. Pon has to pilot the boulders through tight walkways, often fighting against the game’s physics to avoid falling off the ledge. If you do fall, you go right back to the beginning, losing all progress. I got through it, but I worried for the state of my Joy-Con afterwards, with how much stress they were put through.

Tanuki: Pon’s Summer is at its best when it’s as difficult as you want it to be. You can try and pull off some tricks in golf to beat your opponent, or play it safe and have her win. You can make a lousy bartender and call it a day, or you can throw your all into it. You can rack up as many points on the BMX as you like, or ride slow and steady. But when a minigame just can’t find its footing, like riding the boulders in the cave, the game loses track of what makes it work.

At times, it can also feel that the game spreads itself a little too thin. I felt this most in the basic base building. You can unlock a whole lot of items to revamp the Tanuki shrine, but you can’t do too much with them. There’s just not enough freedom, so the plots of land became more of a dumping ground for my trophies.

Tanuki: Pon’s Summer is a cosy game that understands what it means to be a cosy game: create a gorgeous world you want to get lost in, with satisfying but lower-stakes gameplay. By the time I had rebuilt the Tanuki shrine and completed Pon’s summer job, I wanted to dive back in and see more of the townsfolk I’d met along the way. I wanted to keep delivering their mail and nosing my way into their business.

But there were a few sequences in the game I was happy to see the back of, either because they were on the duller side, or just didn’t work with the exaggerated, slapstick control scheme. Equally, I wish Pon’s Summer spent longer on what it does right, letting us go on an infinite number of deliveries around the island, or play as much golf as we please.

#3991. The Petit Planet beta is coming back with new updates, but you still need to hope for an invite

If you've been missing Petit Planet since it was last available to play, you'll be happy to know that HoYoverse is hosting another test soon.

It’s been quite a while since we’ve heard anything about Petit Planet, the upcoming game from Genshin Impact and Honkai: Star Rail developer HoYoverse. By most accounts, Petit Planet is the studio’s take on Animal Crossing, though with a few interesting ideas of its own.

The game’s most recent test took place all the way back in November, but its next big test isn’t far off.

HoYoverse announced today that Petit Planet’s Stardrift Test is scheduled for April 21. This latest build will be available on PC, Android, and iOS. The beta will include new Neighbors, an updated Starsea Voyage, and more for you to do at the Galactic Bazaar.

Seeing as interacting with Neighbors is a core part of this life sim RPG, the confirmation that new faces will be available in this test is big news. Each Neighbor in Petit Planet is a character, with their own personalty and life story.

The Starsea Voyage now includes a map, too, which you can use to take you to other Islets. If you played any of the previous tests, you should already be familiar with this feature.

The only bit of bad news here is that this remains a closed beta. You’re still encouraged to sign up on the official website, but you’re not guaranteed access. HoYoverse said that only a portion of players who sign up will be invited to the upcoming beta.

Petit Planet remains without a release date. If nothing else, it’ll be interesting to see the progress the game has made since last November’s beta.

#3990. Star Wars: Galactic Racer Gets Local Splitscreen Multiplayer Next Year

Star Wars: Galactic Racer has been one of 2026’s breakout titles, but much of the game’s praise stems from its exceptional roguelike single-player mode. If you want to race against human players, you can only do so online. Thankfully, for fans of couch multiplayer, that’s going to change.

Developer Fuse Games announced yesterday that local splitscreen multiplayer is coming to Star Wars: Galactic Racer early next year. The mode lets you race up to three other players on the same screen. That's pretty much all there is to it, but given that local multiplayer was the game's biggest omission and, as a result, the most requested addition, there's probably no better news for Galactic Racer fans.

We’ve heard you! Local split-screen multiplayer racing is coming in early 2027. A dedicated team at Fuse Games has been working hard to develop a new mode: Free Play. Choose your vehicle, character, planet, and track to race alone or with up to 3 other players in local splitscreen action.[image or embed]

Star Wars: Galactic Racer is available now on PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, and PC. Read our review of the game here.

#3989. The Blood of Dawnwalker Patch 1.2 Out Now on PS5, Adds New Game+

As teased towards the end of last week, The Blood of Dawnwalker studio Rebel Wolves has updated its PS5 RPG with a new game+ mode, available to download now.

It's a 4.157GB download, and the option to play the game again whilst carrying over your level, skills, and inventory is the main attraction.

Having finished the RPG's epilogue, you'll unlock new game+. The level cap is raised to 100 in your second playthrough, and the difficulty scaling tied to each region is removed. Enemy levels have been adjusted, and they shall have damage multipliers so combat still presents a challenge.

"In NG+, armor, swords, and accessories will have new versions with updated stats while keeping their original names and icons," the blog post reveals. "You can easily recognize these items by their new frames and the NG+ label next to their names (and for NG+ legendary items – a unique red frame)."

New Game+ becomes a new option on the main menu, and begins after selecting your base game save and difficulty level. You'll then get all your gear at the start of the Withering Away quest in the prologue.

#3988. Heartopia celebrates 30 million downloads with new outfits, permanent price cuts

Heartopia's rise has continued since its launch earlier this year, and the game's developer isn't slowing down with updates.

Heartopia has kicked off a new event to celebrate passing 30 million downloads. Just a couple of weeks after delivering the vintage Hollywood-themed Dreamlight Cinematics event, developer XD Games has revealed The Whimsical Tea Party, a limited-time Gilded Acorn Exhibition.

The event kicked off on Saturday, bringing some new themed content to the game.

Whimsical Tea Party’s biggest addition are the new outfits, including the Wandering Traveler, and the Duke Bunny outfits. Each outfit is available in three different colours. Another thing Heartopia events bring are building materials sets.

This one adds the Labyrinth furniture building materials set, the Hedgehog & Flamingo mallet, and the Cheshire Cat pet costume. Speaking of outfits, XD Games is dropping the in-game prices for a number of items permanently.

All original pet outfits now cost 66.7% less. Those of the Common variety will now cost 10 Souvenir Ticket Stubs, instead of the previous 30. Rare pet outfits will cost 5 Souvenir Ticket Stubs, down from 15.

If you happened to buy Common or Rare original pet outfits between July 17, 2024 and March 22, 2026, you’ll be refunded the difference. This will automatically show up in-game the next time you log in. If you instead purchased those pet outfits between March 23 and April 4, you should look forward to your refund before April 10.

Keeping with the theme of freebies, Heartopia is also celebrating surpassing 30 million downloads worldwide by giving all players a small gift package in-game. This freebie is available until May 29, so you should have enough time to claim it.

For comprehensive guidance on where to find birds, bugs, and fish, check out our Heartopia bird locations, Heartopia bug locations, and Heartopia fish locations guides. If you’re instead looking to find some wild vegetables for those cooking recipes, hit those links. And, as ever, it doesn’t hurt to see if you missed out on any Heartopia codes.

#3987. The Blood Of Dawnwalker Just Got A Free 1.2 Update, Adding New Game Plus

The Blood of Dawnwalker is one of the year's biggest, most ambitious games, and the developers over at Rebel Wolves have done a good job cleaning up bugs and performance issues in the weeks since launch. Today, that trend continued; the new 1.2 update is out now on PS5, Xbox Series X/S, and PC, and it adds New Game Plus.

The new mode is uniquely ideal for a game like Dawnwalker. The narrative is very player-driven, whether it has to do with your literal dialogue options, your ability to manage your vampiric hunger, or the order you complete quests, and all of these elements can cause your experience to vary wildly. It makes sense, then, that players would want to jump back in to try things again and see what might happen if the game is played differently, and New Game Plus allows them to do that while keeping combat fresh.

According to the update notes on the Dawnwalker website, "NG+ unlocks after you complete the game’s Epilogue and lets you experience the story again while keeping your progress – mainly your character level, skills, and inventory." You don't gain access to these skills until you complete the prologue, however, which marks the adventure's proper start.

The new mode will also rebalance the world's level scaling. In the base game, certain areas are much harder than others, but in New Game Plus, all enemies will rise in power to match your level, meaning you can explore the world in whatever order you want. On that note, the level cap has also been raised to 100, and protagonist Coen can collect new, more powerful versions of weapons marked with an "NG+" label.

That's basically everything in this update. Rebel Wolves also added some slight tweaks to combat in the base game and adjusted some geometry in the open world, but the main focus here was New Game Plus. This is in contrast to the 1.1 update, which added a much wider suite of bug fixes and made the game run more smoothly.

#3986. Honkai: Star Rail players are eating good, with Version 4.2 and third anniversary celebrations kicking off later this month

Honkai: Star Rail will be celebrating its third anniversary just days after it delivers a major update, and there's quite a bit to chew on in this one.

HoYoverse just wrapped up a stacked Honkai: Star Rail Special Program, delivering the one-two punch of revealing the game’s next major update, and detailing what you can expect from its third anniversary celebrations.

First off, Version 4.2, dubbed So Laughed the Masses, arrives April 22, making two characters playable, and bringing back a host of beloved characters for re-runs. The new update continues the Phantasmoon Games arc, as the story takes an especially suspect new development.

The big inciting incident of this new chapter is the reveal that whoever wins the Phantasmoon Games will also become the permanent Aeon of Elation. Meanwhile, Fulwish has invited all Supplicants to the Fulwish TV HQ to announce their intention to host a TV debate about the ultimate goal of the Phantasmoon Games.

Naturally, you’re invited, and you’ll have to overcome the challenges that await to gather more Wishpower.

Our first new arrival is Silver Wolf LV.999, with whom you should already be familiar from her Version 1 form. The difference now, of course, is that she’s getting a brand-new alternate kit, since — true to her new name — she's evolved into a Godmode Player upon reaching Level 999. Silver Wolf LV.999 is a 5-Star Imaginary character on the Path of Elation.

Her main combat trick is the ability to rack up Hidden MMR, which is what allows her to eventually activate her Cartridge and settle into the aforementioned Godmode state. While in that form, she shifts the entire battle into the virtual world, pulling in both teams into her gaming domain.

This is essentially a world under her control, which is why she can unlock a Reward Stage at the start of her turn, which lets her spawn in-game items. When picked up, these items can turn the tide of battle.

Keeping up with the ultra-gamer persona, Silver Wolf's Aha Instant strike blasts all enemies with a laser cannon, dealing massive damage. Perhaps her most interesting ability is being able to hack into the battlefield when she’s not actively on the team, something she can do when a teammate falls under enemy control.

Evanescia is the other newly-playable character, who has thus far only been an observer of the Phantasmoon Games, as well as one of the most prominent new characters we've met so far on Planarcadia. V4.2 sees the girl join the roster as a 5-Star Physical character who’s likewise on the Path of Elation. As she fights, she always accumulates Certified Banger, when she earns the title she’s able to simultaneously regenerate Energy and maintain her damage.

Evanescia’s damage continues to increase the more Certified Banger she accumulates, triggering an attack from Master Fox upon reaching a certain threshold, which deals damage to all enemies and regenerates Energy for herself. Her Elation Skill adds a bit of a performance to her kit, and is capable of hitting all enemies.

You may have noticed the Path of Elation theme in this one, so you won’t be surprised to learn that the Elation Trailblazer variant on the main playable character is also joining the team in 4.2. There’s a new weapon that starts off as a glow stick but can transform into a lightblade as you deal damage, and, yes, gain Certified Banger.

It can also turn into nunchucks, which delivers a unique flurry of attacks on all enemies surrounding the character, dealing multiple instances of damage. You can also use it to cheer for a teammate, hyping them up.

Version 4.2 Warp Events will bring back six characters. The first half will see reruns of The Dahlia, Castorice, and Firefly. The second half will give you another shot at unlocking Tribbie, Sunday, and Feixiao. What’s more, four of the game’s characters will be buffed in this update, so you may want to reconsider putting them them back on your team. They are Firefly, Huohuo, Seele, and Welt.

As part of the same update, you can expect the debut of the Cosmic Data Roaming event, which goes live alongside the anniversary celebrations. The event lets you live the life of a streamer.

Currency Wars is getting a big expansion, too. Likewise, the Cosmicon Collective is getting its version 2.0 update, adding new decks, dice as well as a new team challenge game mode.

As for the big third anniversary celebration, it will kick off in-game on April 26, bringing back Festive Gifts. The event will only be available during these celebrations, and it will once again be gifting players who log in regularly a total of 20 pulls.

You’ll also be able to a select a blessing card from a companion of your choice to receive a special gift of 1,600 Stellar Jades. The same celebrations will also seeHuohuo and Robin permanently added to the Stellar Convergence store. You’ll have another chance to exchange a Golden Companion Spirit for any companion you like in that store, too — and all you need to do is log in anytime between Versions 4.2 and 4.4. This being a new year for Honkai: Star Rail, the top-up double bonus is resetting, meaning anyone who tops up their wallet will get a hefty bonus.

Elsewhere, you’ll find new items in the Gift of Stardust Store, including a new outfit for Castorice. Between the time 4.2 launches and when the celebrations begin, you’ll be able to try your luck in Aha's Chosen: Spreading Elation Everywhere, an online event where you can leave a message for a chance to win various prizes.

#3985. Xbox Is Releasing Two First-Party Expansions In December 2026

December is often a very quiet month for new game releases, and that's particularly going to be the case in 2026 due to GTA 6's arrival and the desire from publishers to get as far away from it as possible, but we've still got the likes of Rayman Legends Retold and Stage Tour to look forward to, along with a couple of first-party Xbox expansions.

In terms of first-party stuff, Xbox is initially releasing a paid DLC pack for Minecraft Dungeons 2 on December 1st called The Humblers Awaken. This DLC is included with the Deluxe Edition of the game if you bought it, and it'll be available separately as well.

You can expect "new quests, unexplored environments, colorful cosmetics, and an expanded arsenal of powerful gear" in The Humblers Awaken, while base game players will also be treated to a free update on the same day, adding in new challenges, weapons and armour.

Then, just a day later, Xbox and Obsidian are releasing a first expansion for The Outer Worlds 2, known as Side Effects Guaranteed. This DLC includes a new narrative story (that'll be concluded in the second part next year), a new region of Elysium Valley to explore, new threats, new perks and an increased level cap.

There's also new weapons, armours, outfits, flaws, a new radio station - you get the picture!

Side Effects Guaranteed will cost $14.99 USD when it arrives on December 2nd, or you'll get it included if you bought either the Premium Edition or Premium Upgrade Edition of The Outer Worlds 2.

Perhaps there's a chance we might get even more from Xbox's first-party studios in December, but as mentioned, it's typically a month where the releases die down. In any case, it's nice to see two expansions on the way very soon!

On this page: Xbox Is Releasing Two First-Party Expansions In December 2026

The Sift is in danger! Something ancient is stirring beneath the ground of the new dimension – a threat that has slumbered for ages and is now beginning to wake. Gather your trusty allies, venture deep into unexplored reaches, take on the not-so-happy humblers, and confront the foes behind their rude awakening!

Side Effects Guaranteed is the first chapter of a two-part expansion for The Outer Worlds 2. A distress signal beckons you and your crew of the Incognito to a derelict ship, where you discover the ship’s crew in suspended animation to keep themselves alive, as they’ve been infected with something that causes explosive cell death. The hunt for a cure leads to Elysium Valley, a brand-new region on Eden.

#3983. 'Retire Dragon Quest and Make a New RPG': Drama Surrounds Dragon Quest After Mobile Game Reveal

Square Enix criticised for Toriyama credits

I don't think the future of Dragon Quest has ever seemed so murky.

The timeless series finds itself in a bit of a predicament, with Dragon Quest 12 taking forever to come out, and the tragic passing of franchise artist Akira Toriyama only adding to the surrounding uncertainty.

And while the recent remakes have done well to fill the gap, it does feel like fan patience is becoming stretched for the first time in ages.

Case in point: the newly announced Dragon Quest RPG The Cursed Tree and the Chosen Isle — a mobile spin-off set to launch next year — has been met with a surprising amount of frustration.

Japanese social media has been full of disgruntled fans; some have, again, grown annoyed by the series' relative stagnation, while others have voiced their displeasure over Dragon Quest's continued use of Toriyama's unmistakable art style.

One viral post has a pop at the new mobile game's protagonist, simply pointing out that Toriyama would never have drawn a scabbard that doesn't match its sword's length.

In other words, the quality has fallen off without Toriyama — and yet Square Enix is still crediting him as the character designer.

But what's really caused a fuss is a short blog post by veteran video game composer Yasunori Mitsuda, who worked on Chrono Trigger alongside Toriyama.

In the post, Mitsuda offers his own thoughts on the aforementioned drama. He remains respectful, but it's clear that he's got strong feelings on the state of Dragon Quest as a whole.

"I feel that this direction is not good for the artist, Akira Toriyama fans, and even for the late Akira Toriyama himself," Mitsuda explains.

He continues: "As a personal opinion, since it's impossible to create anything truly new no matter how hard you try, I feel that the Dragon Quest series should be brought to an end, and [series creator Yuji Horii] should create a new RPG."

"What's important is that the game provides dreams, hope, and experiences that can only be had through games to the younger generation of children who will play it in the future. But every time I see topics like this, I realise just how wonderful Dragon Quest is and how it has captivated so many people."

So, what are your thoughts on Dragon Quest at this point in time? Are you feeling similar frustrations? Strike down some slimes in the comments section below.

Nintendo's making sure that everyone has a Switch 2 on their wishlist this Christmas, as it has today announced the 'Nintendo Switch 2 Holiday Experience', which will be coming to select cities in the US over the next month.

Running from 25th November to 23rd December, the pop-up will feature playable demos for a bunch of Switch 2's finest (Pokopia, Mario Kart World, Ocarina of Time, Splatoon Raiders, and more), and give you a chance to see them all in both handheld and docked mode.

The event will also feature a Nintendo Holiday Gift Guide — because you know kids will leave this one wanting a console of their own — and all attendees can 'check in' at the My Nintendo station to redeem a gift tag set and 100 Platinum Points.

#3981. Animal Crossing: New Horizons gets a new item to celebrate 25 years of the series

The allegedly finished game might finally, truly be feature complete with the addition of an anniversary item.

Animal Crossing: New Horizons has received a surprise patch today to celebrate the 25th anniversary of the life sim series. The update, version 3.0.2, is available across the Switch and Switch 2 versions of the game.

The patch brings a single new addition to New Horizons - a leaf item. Everyone gets it, too, so you don’t have to do anything special to acquire it.

After installing the patch, simply head to your in-house mailbox to claim it. The mail includes a hearty message to fans who supported the series for years, featuring an appropriate Nintendo N64 stamp.

The Leaf Statue, as it’s referred to in-game, lights up when placed.

April 14, 2011 marks the release of the original, lesser-known version of Animal Crossing in Japan. The game was initially released as Animal Forest (Dobutsu no Mori) on the Nintendo N64, before later making its way to the Nintendo GameCube in December of the same year as Dobutsu no Mori+ with some extra features.

That same, original design of the package is also available for display in your game. The rest of the patch notes are entirely about various bug fixes, so not much more there. You can see the full change log on Nintendo’s support website.

#3980. Civilization Developer Firaxis Lays Off A Third Of Its Staff

Firaxis, the studio behind the Civilization series, has laid off around 60 employees, representing a third of its staff. The report comes from Bloomberg’s Jason Schreier.

In a statement provided to Bloomberg by a spokesperson from 2K, a subsidiary of Firaxis' owner, Take-Two, “Firaxis is restructuring and recentering around the studio’s core strength—designing world class strategy games that have set the industry standard for the genre for the last 30 years. As part of these changes, the size of the studio is being reduced to focus on design, technology and the player experience, which means saying goodbye to talented colleagues who helped build Firaxis. These decisions are never easy, but they’re essential to build the next chapter of Firaxis.”

In addition to the 60 affected staffers, Firaxis studio head Heather Hazen is also departing. Bloomberg also reports, via anonymous Firaxis employees speaking to the outlet, that the studio is working on an unannounced XCOM game that has had a challenging development, with the team recently missing an important development milestone. This project, if it releases, will be the first Firaxis-developed XCOM game since XCOM: Chimera Squad in 2020.

Firaxis’ most recent release is Civilization VII, which launched in February 2025 to favorable reviews but initially "slow" sales, according to Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick last August.  The game currently has a Mixed reception on Steam after Firaxis spent the last year updating the game to address player complaints. Before Civilization VII, Firaxis shipped Marvel's Midnight Suns in 2022, another critically well-received game that failed to meet sales expectations.

#3979. Metro 2039 goes back to its Metro underground roots, with a story shaped by the war in Ukraine and the people who suffer it

Metro 2039 takes us back to the tunnels of the Moscow Metro where, fittingly, Nazi ideology never died.

The Metro series is finally, officially back with a new installment. 4A Games has just unveiled Metro 2039 to the world, the follow-up to the outstanding Metro Exodus, released all the way back in 2019.

2039 takes an unusual route with its scope, however. Rather than build on the semi-open-world structure of Exodus, the upcoming sequel instead brings the focus back to where it all began: the Metro.

What won’t be changing is the kind of game that it is. Metro 2039 remains, like its predecessors, a story-driven, single-player game. Returning to the confined spaces of the Moscow Metro brings the focus back to the claustrophobic, uneasy atmosphere of the original games.

The game’s protagonist is, for the first time, going to be voiced throughout. From what we’ve been able to see, the psychological horror in this installment will be driven more by the very real effects the apocalypse has had, and continues to have, on denizens of the Metro.

2039 has been in development for years, but 4A Games has been rocked by two considerable events: the 2020 Covid pandemic, and Russia’s 2022 invasion of Ukraine, where the developer is based. The game’s darker story has changed in response to that.

The team’s Ukrainian perspective is molded into the narrative, and more prominently represents the toll the events of the last several years has taken on members of the team, their families and communities.

According to the developer, you can expect a bigger emphasis on choice and consequence, with Russian author Dmitry Glukhovsky returning to co-write a narrative that explores the compromised morality of a post-war society.

The new protagonist’s return to the Metro comes with the reveal that the different underground factions are now united under one banner, the not-so-subtly named Novoreich. Lead by a former Spartan, the Novoreich is an authoritarian regime which offers what it believes to be the only path to salvation.

4A Games remains majority Ukrainian, with teams based in Kyiv, and Malta. Unlike most AAA projects today, the studio continues to rely on its own engine tech. The 4A Engine is given a major upgrade for 2039: ray tracing is now a core component of the rendering pipeline, but the tech has been rebuilt to run better on modern hardware.

Today’s reveal sadly didn’t feature much gameplay - only a brief first-look with a mix of gameplay and cinematics. The developer, however, emphasised that creating cluttered, believable and lived-in environments remains a key focus.

Metro 2039 is set for release sometime this winter on PC, Xbox Series X/S, and PS5.

#3978. Blizzard will talk about Diablo 4: Lord of Hatred one last time before the expansion's launch next week

We're well under two weeks from the launch of Diablo 4's next expansion, Lord of Hatred, but there's more yet to be said.

Diablo 4 is mere days away from the launch of its biggest expansion yet, and Blizzard wants to make sure it got one last chance to tell you about it. Lord of Hatred is the follow-up to 2024’s Vessel of Hatred, and it’s set to arrive on April 28.

Next week, however, we’re getting an updated look at the new content as part of a livestream. This is the Developer Update kind; the meaty, information-dense show anyone who follows Diablo’s livestreams should be familiar with.

The next Developer Update is set for Thursday, April 23. It’ll kick off at 11am PT, 2pm ET, 6pm GMT. The show will, naturally, focus on Lord of Hatred. In particular, we’re getting another look at the expansion content that hasn’t been given the same level of coverage as the bigger features.

Everyone knows about the new Skovos region, the Warlock class (and the Paladin before that), but we haven’t seen much from the other gameplay-altering features that affect a lot of the core flow.

In next week’s showcase, Blizzard will show off the updated and expanded skill trees - which come to all classes, the Talisman system, and the gear-altering Horadric Cube. War Plans, the new make-your-own-endgame feature will be discussed, too.

More interestingly, we’re also going to hear about the new season kicking off right alongside the launch of Lord of Hatred. A short, in-betweener season is currently live in Diablo 4, and it’s going to end right as the next one/the expansion launch.

And, of course, the show won’t end before the team takes a few questions from chat, as is tradition. If you want to catch it live, you’ll be able to do so on Diablo’s official YouTube, Twitch, Twitter, and TikTok channels.

#3976. GDC Survey Suggests Devs Want To Make Games For Switch 2 More Than PS5 Or Xbox

The GDC Festival of Gaming has published its latest 'State of the Game Industry' report, which is based on a survey of over 2,600 game industry professionals on topics such as AI, layoffs, labour, and more.

One particular result caught our eye, and it's regarding which platforms developers are currently interested in developing for in the future. As expected, PC was comfortably the winner at 81%, likely down to its versatility, ease-of-use, and broad visibility of storefronts like Steam and Epic Games Store.

However, it's the Switch 2 that bagged the silver medal at 46%, putting it ahead of the PS5, Xbox Series X|S, Steam Deck, Steam Machine, and even upcoming consoles like the PS6 and Project Helix.

Since its release in June 2025, the Switch 2 has seen a staggering number of releases, from high-profile 'AAA' titles to smaller indie games, and it seems this is only set to continue or perhaps even accelerate in the future.

In a similar chart looking at which platform(s) developers' upcoming game or project will ship on next, the Switch 2 ranks lower than PC, PS5, Xbox Series X|S, and Steam Deck, pulling in 29% of the vote. With this one, however, it's worth considering external factors that might be at play.

For example, it's easy to say that you want to develop for the Switch 2, but whether you have the budget and dev kits to actually do so is another question. Just something to consider when looking at these results.

#3974. The Sims 4's much maligned paid mods have made it to consoles, but Kits are coming back to PC

The Sims 4's Marketplace and user-created content have officially arrived on consoles, a little over a month after their debut on PC.

The Sims 4 players on PlayStation and Xbox have now caught up to their friends on PC, at least when it comes to the game’s Marketplace. This new feature is essentially a hub for paid mods and other user-created content.

As often happens when long-established games introduce paid mods, The Sims 4’s wasn’t especially well-received, in part because of the introduction of a new premium currency - Moola - that is the only way to purchase any of that content.

The Moola denominations and prices are similar to many other in-game currencies, and the criticism around them is the same: they obfuscate the true value of items, and because of the way those denominations are structured, you’ll never be able to buy exactly what you need.

For most games, the subject of paid mods has always been fraught, and that's certainly true for The Sims 4. In the announcement blog post, Maxis said that the launch on consoles will work similarly to what PC players have seen, in that Kits will no longer be available to buy directly with real money on the PlayStation and Microsoft Stores. While Expansion Packs, Game Packs, and Stuff Packs will remain, you’ll need to buy Moola if you want to acquire Kits going forward.

Interestingly, however, EA seems to have changed its mind somewhat on the Kits situation. A recently leaked memo (via SimsCommunity), appears to show that the publisher intends on making Kits available for purchase directly again, without the need for Moola.

Unfortunately, this only appears to affect the PC version, with the reversion reportedly forthcoming on both the EA App as well as Steam. Indeed, according to the same report, the change has already taken place on the former, with the latter following on April 20.

Considering the Marketplace only just launched on consoles, the company may wait to see if the decision to remove Kits from console platform marketplaces will be as poorly received as it has been on PC.

If you’re looking to jump back into The Sims 4 to check out all the new paid content, make sure you’re well-equipped with our list of Sims 4 cheats and debug options, or this one specifically for the Royalty & Legacy expansion cheats.

#3973. Xbox Announces Black Friday Sale 2026, Reveals Nine Included Games

Earlier this month, we mentioned that Xbox's Black Friday Sale for 2026 was set to begin on November 19th according to a leak, and now Microsoft has officially announced that it will indeed start showing up as of this Thursday.

The leak mentioned it had a start time of 3pm EST, but Xbox actually says that it'll be 9pm PST / 12pm EST / 5am GMT on November 19th going into November 20th, so you might need to hang around a bit longer until the deals appear.

"The best time to grab a gift for gamers is launching on November 19 at 9 PM PST. During our Black Friday sale, save up to 80% on select XBOX and PC games, and check out discounts on select XBOX accessories."

We also have nine confirmed games for this Xbox Black Friday Sale, which are as follows:

If you're a bit underwhelmed by what you're seeing here, don't worry - over 2,000 games will be included in the full Xbox Black Friday Sale, and despite Xbox suggesting they'll be "up to 80% off", we know from past experience that the sale will include discounts of 90% off and even 95% off for some games.

We'll obviously have a whole bunch of Xbox Black Friday roundups for you beginning later this week on Pure Xbox, but we should also mention that Microsoft is promoting discounts on various Xbox accessories (like controllers and Xbox Design Lab purchases) for the Black Friday period, along with a special Samsung TV deal that includes a free Xbox Nano controller along with two months of Xbox Game Pass Ultimate.

Sit tight, and we'll be back with all the big highlights from the Xbox Black Friday game sale in a couple of days' time!

#3972. Naval warfare, an actual server browser and more on the way to Battlefield 6 this year as BF Studios reveals 2026 roadmap

2026 is looking very exciting for Battlefield 6, even if much of what's coming is based on things we already know, and some we've long been asking for.

It took Battlefield Studios over four months to tell Battlefield 6 players what they can actually expect from the game over the course of this year, in terms of content - but we’re glad to see a plan laid out nonetheless.

The developer unveiled a grand 2026 roadmap, covering three more seasons currently in the works, and a wealth of new additions across the entire game, including new maps and the introduction of a new theatre of combat.

In a wide-ranging new video dubbed The Year Ahead, members of the Battlefield 6 development team have revealed a lot of new information about the future of the multiplayer shooter, going over plenty of the features and new content coming over the course of this year.

The video confirmed that BF6 has at least three other seasons in the works. Season 3, which begins in May, will be followed by Season 4, and Season 5 later in the year. Season 5 is the most mysterious, which is understandable.

We’ve known about some of what’s coming in Season 3, such as the remake of Golmud Railway (now called Railway to Golmud), but the video also revealed that a remake of Battlefield 3’s Grand Bazaar - now Cairo Bazaar - will also arrive later in the same season. Other exciting additions, such as battle royale solos and ranked play for Redsec are also on the agenda for Season 3.

Season 4, set for July, looks to be the biggest so far, with the introduction of naval combat, which will be available across two maps. Tsuru Reef, which is said to be even larger than Golmud, the largest map in BF6. The Pacific-set map won’t be the only one, as later in the season, another remake will arrive, this time of the iconic Wake Island.

The introduction of naval combat will bring with it a new dynamic wave system, aircraft carriers with operational flight decks, and new naval vehicles. Custom lobbies and Spectator Mode are also planned for Season 4.

Season 5 will bring three maps to BF6, rather than two, but all of its content remains under wraps.

Perhaps a sour note is that almost all of the maps referenced and shown in the video are remakes of maps from other Battlefield games, or reimagined at the very least. The Battlefield series is no stranger to remaking its own maps, but Battlefield 6 appears to be leaning on it much more than past entries.

If it’s any consolation, however, the map remakes we’ve played so far in Battlefield 6 have gone through major changes that have contributed to giving them a different flow and feel from their classic versions, or even remakes in other BF games.

Over the course of 2026, you can also expect the return of persistent servers, as well as a server browser to find them all - just like the good ol’ days. This includes the ability to host your own, though it’s unclear quite how this is going to work.

Season 3 is set to revealed in the coming days, so you’ll be hearing back from BF Studios in the near future.
